title: Bidegree expansion of a conjugated total oplax comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_0,\mathcal A_1,\mathcal B_0,\mathcal B_1$ be abelian monoidal categories [def-sp-abelian, def-sfb-monoidal-category], small relative to a fixed containing universe. Assume their tensors are additive in each variable, all small colimits exist, and tensoring on either side preserves them [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $E_j:\mathcal A_j\to\mathcal B_j$ ($j=0,1$) be additive strong monoidal equivalences, and let $F_{\mathrm i}:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal A_1$ and $F_{\mathrm s}:\mathcal B_0\to\mathcal B_1$ be additive strong monoidal functors preserving countable coproducts [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Fix an arbitrary natural isomorphism $a:E_1F_{\mathrm i}\cong F_{\mathrm s}E_0$, not assumed monoidal. For each of these functors $G$ write $\gamma^G_{M,N}:G(M\otimes N)\cong GM\otimes GN$ for its inverse tensorator and $\epsilon^G:G\mathbf1\cong\mathbf1$ for its oplax unit. Use unbounded integer cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their signed direct-sum tensor total [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], and the associator and unitors induced from the ordinary ones [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. Extend functors and $a$ termwise. Write $T_G:G\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(GP\otimes GQ)$ for the canonical preserved-coproduct comparison with summand maps $\gamma^G_{P^p,Q^q}$, and $j_G:G(\mathbf1[0])\cong\mathbf1[0]$ for $\epsilon^G$ in degree zero and the canonical zero-object comparisons elsewhere. Define
$$\widetilde\gamma_{M,N}=(a_M\otimes a_N)\,\gamma^{E_1}_{F_{\mathrm i}M,F_{\mathrm i}N}\,E_1(\gamma^{F_{\mathrm i}}_{M,N})\,a_{M\otimes N}^{-1}\,F_{\mathrm s}((\gamma^{E_0}_{M,N})^{-1}),$$
and define the chain isomorphism
$$A_{P,Q}=(a_P\otimes a_Q)\,T_{E_1}\,E_1(T_{F_{\mathrm i}})\,a_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}^{-1}\,F_{\mathrm s}(T_{E_0}^{-1}):F_{\mathrm s}\operatorname{Tot}(E_0P\otimes E_0Q)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}(F_{\mathrm s}E_0P\otimes F_{\mathrm s}E_0Q).$$
Composition in these formulas is from right to left.
For every integer $n$, the set $I_n=\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$ is countable and is small in the containing universe. The functors $E_0,E_1,F_{\mathrm i},F_{\mathrm s}$ carry each degree-$n$ tensor coproduct cocone to a coproduct cocone. If $\kappa_G:\bigoplus_{I_n}GZ_{p,q}\cong G(\bigoplus_{I_n}Z_{p,q})$ is the canonical comparison induced by the images of the injections, then $\kappa_G^{-1}G(\iota_{p,q})$ is the corresponding injection. Let $\iota_{p,q}:E_0P^p\otimes E_0Q^q\to\operatorname{Tot}(E_0P\otimes E_0Q)^n$ and let $\iota'_{p,q}$ be the target-total injection. The full conjugation, with these canonical coproduct comparisons, satisfies
$$A_{P,Q}^nF_{\mathrm s}(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}\widetilde\gamma_{P^p,Q^q}\qquad(p+q=n).$$
These component formulas give a natural chain map: its differential equation is the sum of the ordinary naturality equations with $(d_P^p,1)$ and $(1,d_Q^q)$, the second multiplied by $(-1)^p$. No boundedness or exactness of $F_{\mathrm i},F_{\mathrm s}$ is assumed.

proof.text: The maps $p\mapsto(p,n-p)$ and $(p,q)\mapsto p$ are inverse bijections $\mathbf Z\cong I_n$, so $I_n$ is countable and small in the containing universe. By [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], $E_0,E_1$ preserve the coproducts indexed by the discrete category on $I_n$; $F_{\mathrm i},F_{\mathrm s}$ preserve them by hypothesis. Thus each image cocone is a coproduct cocone. For any of these $G$ and any such family $Z$, coproduct uniqueness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] constructs $\kappa_G$ with $\kappa_G\iota^G_{p,q}=G(\iota^Z_{p,q})$, and constructs its inverse with $\kappa_G^{-1}G(\iota^Z_{p,q})=\iota^G_{p,q}$. The two composites are identities because their restrictions to every injection are identities. This proves both the preservation assertion and the claimed canonical comparison formula.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact, applied to equivalences; canonical coproduct comparison from its universal property

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal] separately to $E_0,E_1,F_{\mathrm i},F_{\mathrm s}$. Step 1 supplies countable coproduct preservation for the equivalences; additivity, strong monoidality and the tensor/colimit hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses here. Its $\tau$ is the specified $T_G$, since both satisfy $T_G^nG(\iota)=\iota'\gamma^G$. It gives natural chain isomorphisms $T_G$ and the stated $j_G$ (its unit $e_G^{-1}$ is our $\epsilon^G$). Termwise $a$ is a natural chain isomorphism: its chain equation is precisely naturality of $a$ at each differential, and its inverse satisfies the equation by cancellation. Additivity makes termwise functors act on complexes and their maps [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The tensor of the two chain isomorphisms $a_P,a_Q$ is the chain isomorphism with summand maps $a_{P^p}\otimes a_{Q^q}$, by the tensor construction [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Consequently all five factors defining $A$ are natural chain isomorphisms with the indicated source and target.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes; single-functor extension supplied by lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal

proof.text:
Fix $p+q=n$. Put $X=P^p\otimes Q^q$, $C=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$ and write $u:X\to C^n$, $v:E_0P^p\otimes E_0Q^q\to\operatorname{Tot}(E_0P\otimes E_0Q)^n$ for the injections. Let $w:F_{\mathrm i}P^p\otimes F_{\mathrm i}Q^q\to\operatorname{Tot}(F_{\mathrm i}P\otimes F_{\mathrm i}Q)^n$. The summand formula of [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal], multiplied by the two inverse isomorphisms, gives
$$(T_{E_0}^{-1})^n v=E_0(u)(\gamma^{E_0}_{P^p,Q^q})^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $a$ at $u$, with the invertible components cancelled, gives
$$a_{C^n}^{-1}F_{\mathrm s}(E_0(u))=E_1F_{\mathrm i}(u)a_X^{-1}.$$
Finally $T_{F_{\mathrm i}}^nF_{\mathrm i}(u)=w\gamma^{F_{\mathrm i}}_{P^p,Q^q}$ by the same cited summand formula. Applying functoriality to these three equalities computes the first three factors, in order of application:
$$E_1(T_{F_{\mathrm i}})^n a_{C^n}^{-1}F_{\mathrm s}((T_{E_0}^{-1})^n)F_{\mathrm s}(v)
=E_1(w)E_1(\gamma^{F_{\mathrm i}}_{P^p,Q^q})a_X^{-1}F_{\mathrm s}((\gamma^{E_0}_{P^p,Q^q})^{-1}).$$
All compositions are right to left; $a_C^n=a_{C^n}$ because the extension is termwise.

source.place: Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex; explicit agent calculation of the functor-square comparison

proof.text:
Let $t:E_1F_{\mathrm i}P^p\otimes E_1F_{\mathrm i}Q^q\to\operatorname{Tot}(E_1F_{\mathrm i}P\otimes E_1F_{\mathrm i}Q)^n$ be the next injection. The remaining total comparison satisfies
$$T_{E_1}^nE_1(w)=t\gamma^{E_1}_{F_{\mathrm i}P^p,F_{\mathrm i}Q^q}$$
by [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal]. The tensor-map formula in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] gives
$$(a_P\otimes a_Q)^nt=\iota'_{p,q}(a_{P^p}\otimes a_{Q^q}).$$
Substitute these into step 3. The resulting coefficient map after $\iota'_{p,q}$ is exactly the five-factor definition of $\widetilde\gamma_{P^p,Q^q}$, hence $A_{P,Q}^nF_{\mathrm s}(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}\widetilde\gamma_{P^p,Q^q}$. Every equality used canonical injections, so no additional identification of coproducts occurs. Since the $F_{\mathrm s}(\iota_{p,q})$ form a coproduct cocone by step 1, these restrictions determine $A^n$ uniquely [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex; explicit agent calculation of the functor-square comparison

proof.text: Each of the five ordinary factors is natural: use tensorator naturality for E₀, naturality of a inverse at f tensor g, oplax tensorator naturality for Fi and E₁, and tensor the naturality equations for a at f and g. This proves the ordinary conjugated comparison is natural. For naturality on complexes, check after every Fs image of a tensor injection, which is sufficient by the preserved coproduct universal property. The tensor-map injection formula, the summand expansion in Steps 3–4 and ordinary naturality identify the two sides. For the signed equation, replace the component map by Fs of the source injection followed by the degree component of the already constructed chain isomorphism A. Its chain-map equation moves the target differential before A. Functoriality identifies the resulting composite with Fs applied to the source injection followed by the source tensor differential. Expand this differential using the signed total formula of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Additivity of Fs preserves its sum and the (-1)^p coefficient. Apply the summand expansion separately at (p+1,q) and (p,q+1); this is exactly the required signed equation. Only two terms occur, for all integer degrees. No boundedness, exactness, symmetry, or monoidality of a is used.
